features.feature_value: Avoided posts with inflammatory language to prevent unproductive political conversation.
features.rationale: The participant explicitly links avoiding removal/keeping decisions to presence of inflammatory language.

features.feature_value: Looked for any sign of a threat; treated the pair as mutual blame/finger-pointing and rejected both.
features.evidence_span: "looking for any sign of what could be deemed as a threat"
features.rationale: Their decision depends on whether the content contains threatening elements.

features.feature_value: Kept posts if coherent and civil; canceled if incoherent, inflammatory, and bigoted.
features.rationale: They provide a clear two-part content quality threshold for keep vs remove.

features.feature_value: Main criterion was disallowing foul language; viewed it as inappropriate for online debate.
features.evidence_span: "I did not allow any foul language"
features.rationale: They state foul language alone was the key keeping/rejecting rule.

features.feature_value: Believed profanity and aggressive discussion is poor conduct for getting a point across.
features.rationale: They tie removal/avoidance to profanity/aggressive tone as a normative criterion.

features.feature_value: Eliminated both posts when language was harmful/inflammatory; pairs eliminated were often extreme.
features.rationale: They describe making the same removal choice for both versions based on harmful/inflammatory cues and extremity.

features.feature_value: Focused on the value of the discussion; rejected when it was just bashing with no valid points/debate value.
features.rationale: Their criterion is whether the pair produces value beyond interpersonal attacks.

features.feature_value: Allowed content as long as it was not offensive, invoking respect for free speech.
features.rationale: They articulate a boundary condition for inclusion: free speech broadly, exclusion when offensive.
